notes.md: - **Reserved items, 2007-08:** **125** items dereserved on **13 March 2007**, leaving **114**; **79** more dereserved in **Feb 2008**, leaving **35**.

- **NSIC (National Small Industries Corporation):** set up **1955**; Miniratna CPSE under the **Ministry of MSME**; HQ **New Delhi**; marketing, raw-material and credit support for small industry products.
- **MUDRA:** launched **8 April 2015** as a **wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI**; refinances micro loans given by banks, NBFCs and MFIs.

new.s: What was the name of the first successful cotton mill set up by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar at Bombay in 1854?
new.x: Davar's Bombay Spinning and Weaving Co. at Tardeo (7 July 1854) was India's first successful cotton mill.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: first cotton mill -> company name

new.s: When was the foundation stone of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL) laid?
new.x: The foundation stone of RINL, Visakhapatnam (built with USSR help), was laid on 20 January 1971.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: RINL foundation stone date

new.s: Which public-sector steel plant was India's fourth integrated steel plant?
new.x: Bokaro (Jharkhand), built with USSR help, was the fourth integrated plant after Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: Bokaro 4th integrated plant

new.s: Up to what amount can a Miniratna Category-II CPSE invest without Government approval?
o: ₹500 crore or equal to net worth
new.x: Miniratna-II CPSEs can invest up to ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth without Government approval.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: Miniratna-II investment limit

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Miniratna Category-I CPSE must have made a pre-tax profit of ₹30 crore or more in at least one of the three years.
2. A Miniratna Category-II CPSE can invest up to ₹300 crore or 50% of its net worth without Government approval.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Miniratna-I needs ₹30 crore+ pre-tax profit in one year; Miniratna-II's limit is ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: Miniratna criteria and limits

new.s: Which CPSE was given Miniratna Category-I status in July 2026?
new.x: MECON became a Miniratna Category-I CPSE in July 2026; NALCO, NHPC and BEL are Navratnas.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: MECON Miniratna-I (2026)

new.s: Under which Ministry does NALCO, the Navratna aluminium company headquartered at Bhubaneswar, function?
new.x: NALCO (1981, Bhubaneswar) is a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Mines.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: NALCO ministry

new.s: Under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries, which industry has the lowest weight?
new.x: Fertilisers have the lowest weight (2.73%) in the new series, as in the old one.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: lowest core weight (new series)

new.s: What is the weight of mining in the new IIP series with base year 2022-23?
new.x: In the new IIP, manufacturing has 76.1%, mining 11.1%, electricity and gas 10.9%, water supply 2.02%.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: mining weight in IIP

new.s: What was the share of industry (secondary sector) in Andhra Pradesh's GSVA in 2025-26?
new.x: Industry's share of AP's GSVA was 21.16% in 2024-25 and 21.57% in 2025-26.
new.angle: U0505 notes gap: AP industry share 2025-26

new.s: From 1 April 2025, what are the investment and turnover limits of a micro enterprise?
new.x: The limits raised from 1 April 2025 make a micro unit one with investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: micro limits from 2025

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the MSME limits in force from 1 April 2025:
1. A micro enterprise may invest up to ₹2.5 crore.
2. The turnover ceiling of a micro enterprise is ₹15 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The micro investment limit is ₹2.5 crore; the turnover ceiling is ₹10 crore, not ₹15 crore.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: micro limits from 2025

new.s: Which committee, set up in 2001, dealt with credit access for the small-scale sector?
new.x: The S.P. Gupta Committee (2001) studied credit access for SSIs.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: S.P. Gupta Committee 2001

new.s: In which year did the TReDS platforms for discounting MSME invoices start?
new.x: TReDS, the RBI-regulated online invoice discounting system (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart), started in 2017.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: TReDS year

new.s: Under PMEGP, up to what rate of margin-money subsidy can women beneficiaries get?
new.x: PMEGP gives special categories such as women a subsidy of up to 35%.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: PMEGP women subsidy

new.s: For up to how many years from incorporation can a deep-tech entity be recognised as a startup under Startup India?
new.x: Ordinary startups are recognised up to 10 years; deep-tech startups up to 20 years (turnover up to ₹300 crore).
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: deep-tech startup limits

new.s: What daily stipend is paid during training under PM Vishwakarma?
new.x: PM Vishwakarma pays artisans in 18 trades a stipend of ₹500 per day during training.
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: PM Vishwakarma stipend

new.s: In FY26 (up to 1 December 2025), what share of procurement by central ministries and CPSEs came from MSEs?
new.x: Against the 25% target, procurement from MSEs reached 44.76% in FY26 (to 1 Dec 2025).
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: procurement achieved FY26

new.s: To what level did the Industrial Policy of 1991 raise the investment limit for ancillary units?
new.x: The 1991 policy raised the ancillary limit from ₹45 lakh to ₹75 lakh (small units ₹35 lakh to ₹60 lakh).
new.angle: U0506 notes gap: 1991 ancillary limit

new.s: How many items remained reserved for the small-scale sector after 125 items were dereserved on 13 March 2007?
new.x: The March 2007 dereservation of 125 items left 114 items reserved for micro and small enterprises.
new.angle: U0506 PYQ y9a61a7a667a web: reserved items in 2007

new.s: In February 2008, 79 more items were dereserved. How many items then remained reserved for micro and small enterprises?
new.x: Removing 79 items from the list of 114 left only 35 reserved items (Feb 2008).
new.angle: U0506 PYQ y9a61a7a667a web: reserved items 2008

new.s: In which year was the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) set up?
new.x: NSIC was set up by the Government of India in 1955; it works under the Ministry of MSME.
new.angle: U0506 PYQ ybcd3eb777b8 web: NSIC year

new.s: MUDRA was set up as a wholly owned subsidiary of which institution?
new.x: MUDRA was set up in 2015 as a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI to refinance loans to micro units.
new.angle: U0506 PYQ y7f85c41d35f web: MUDRA parent

new.s: When was the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana launched?
new.x: PMMY and MUDRA were launched by the Prime Minister on 8 April 2015.
new.angle: U0506 PYQ y7f85c41d35f web: MUDRA launch

new.s: Which industrial policy statement first identified a list of 'core sector' industries?
new.x: The 1973 statement drew up a core sector list and tightened MRTP.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: 1973 core sector list

new.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, how many industries were placed in the centrally regulated category?
new.x: IPR 1948 put 18 industries (salt, automobiles, cement, sugar, textiles etc.) under Central regulation; 6 were in the mixed sector.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: IPR 1948 regulated industries

new.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, in which schedule was aluminium placed?
o: It was kept outside all schedules
new.x: Schedule B (12 industries) included aluminium, machine tools, ferro-alloys and basic chemicals.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: IPR 1956 Schedule B contents

new.s: For how long is the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 valid?
o: Five years or till a new policy is notified
new.x: Policy 4.0 (G.O.Ms.No.68, 26 Oct 2024) is valid for five years (2024-29) or till a new policy.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: AP policy validity (#6)

new.s: What capital subsidy does the Andhra Pradesh MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 give to general MSMEs?
new.x: The policy gives a 25% capital subsidy, rising to 45% for special categories.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: AP MSME policy subsidy

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29:
1. It aims to have one AP port among the world's top 20 by 2047.
2. Its nodal agency is APIIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The policy aims at a top-20 world port by 2047; its nodal agency is the AP Maritime Board, not APIIC.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: AP Maritime Policy aims

new.s: What share of India's port cargo does the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29 aim to handle?
new.x: The policy aims for AP to handle 20% of India's port cargo.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: AP Maritime Policy cargo share

new.s: What is the period of Andhra Pradesh's Aerospace and Defence Policy 4.0?
new.x: The Aerospace and Defence and Space 4.0 policies cover 2025-30; most other 4.0 policies cover 2024-29.
new.angle: U0507 notes gap: AP aerospace policy period

new.s: Under which Ministry did the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) function?
new.x: BIFR came under the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.
new.angle: U0508 notes gap: BIFR ministry

new.s: Under the original SICA, 1985, which condition made a company sick?
o: Accumulated losses equal to or more than its net worth
A fall of 50% in net profit
An NPA account for three months
new.x: SICA 1985 treated a company (registered 7+ years) as sick if accumulated losses equalled or exceeded its net worth.
new.angle: U0508 notes gap: SICA loss test (#2)

new.s: Who headed the early committee on disinvestment set up in 1991?
new.x: The V. Krishnamurthy Committee (1991) set the early approach; Rangarajan came in 1993.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: Krishnamurthy Committee 1991

new.s: When was the Department of Disinvestment set up?
new.x: The Department of Disinvestment was set up on 10 December 1999 and renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: Department of Disinvestment date

new.s: Under which department does the National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC) function?
new.x: NLMC (3 June 2022) works under DPE and monetises surplus land of CPSEs.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: NLMC department

new.s: How much penalty did the Competition Commission of India impose on Google in 2022?
new.x: CCI fined Google ₹1,337 crore in 2022 for abuse of dominance (Android).
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: CCI Google case

new.s: On which company did the Competition Commission of India impose a penalty of ₹213.14 crore in 2024?
new.x: CCI fined Meta ₹213.14 crore (2024) over WhatsApp's privacy policy; NCLAT upheld the fine in 2025.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: CCI Meta case

new.s: From when did merger (combination) control under the Competition Act, 2002 come into force?
new.x: Anti-competitive provisions came into force on 20 May 2009 and combination control from June 2011.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: merger control date

new.s: Against a target of ₹2,500 crore, how much was realised from disinvestment in 1991-92, the first year?
new.x: In 1991-92 disinvestment in 31 PSUs yielded ₹3,038 crore, more than the ₹2,500 crore target.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: 1991-92 realisation

new.s: Which company acquired Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited (NINL) through strategic sale?
new.x: NINL was sold to Tata Steel; the sale brought no proceeds to the exchequer.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: NINL buyer

new.s: In which year was the LIC IPO, then India's biggest IPO, listed?
new.x: The LIC IPO listed on 17 May 2022 and was the biggest IPO at the time.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: LIC IPO year

new.s: Under which section of the Companies Act, 2013 was the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) set up?
new.x: NCLT was set up under Section 408 (on 1 June 2016); NCLAT under Section 410.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: NCLT section

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, to what level may the Government's stake in listed CPSEs be reduced?
new.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 says the stake in listed CPSEs may fall to 26%.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: ES 2025-26 CPSE stake

new.s: Under the original MRTP Act, 1969, an undertaking was covered if its assets were at least how much?
new.x: Originally MRTP covered firms with assets of ₹20 crore+ or a 33% market share; it was raised to ₹100 crore in 1984-85.
new.angle: U0509 notes gap: original MRTP threshold

new.s: About how many startups had been recognised under Startup India by August 2026?
new.x: Recognised startups grew from 502 in 2016 to about 2.47 lakh by August 2026.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: Startup India count

new.s: What is the outlay of the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 approved on 15 July 2026?
new.x: ISM 2.0 was approved with ₹1,27,500 crore; ISM 1.0 had ₹76,000 crore.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: ISM 2.0 outlay

new.s: Up to what share of project cost does the India Semiconductor Mission give as capital assistance?
new.x: ISM gives up to 50% capital assistance for fabs, OSAT/ATMP and design.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: ISM capital assistance

new.s: With which company is Tata Electronics setting up the semiconductor wafer fab at Dholera, Gujarat?
new.x: The Dholera fab is a Tata Electronics-PSMC (Taiwan) project worth ₹91,526 crore.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: Dholera fab partner

new.s: In which State is India's first advanced 3D packaging unit?
new.x: Of the ISM 1.0 projects, the first advanced 3D packaging unit is in Odisha.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: 3D packaging unit -> State

new.s: How many jobs had the PLI schemes created by September 2025?
new.x: By Sept 2025 PLI brought over ₹2.0 lakh crore investment and 12.60 lakh jobs.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: PLI jobs

new.s: Which scheme does the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31) replace?
o: PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
new.x: The ₹62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme replaces PLI-LSEM.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: mobile scheme replaces PLI-LSEM

new.s: To what amount was the outlay of the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) raised in Budget 2026-27?
new.x: Budget 2026-27 raised ECMS from ₹22,919 crore to ₹40,000 crore.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: ECMS outlay

new.s: What was the value of mobile phone production in India in 2024-25?
new.x: Mobile output rose from ₹18,900 crore (2014-15) to ₹5.45 lakh crore (2024-25).
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: mobile production value

new.s: Which was India's largest export category in 2025?
new.x: Smartphones became India's largest export category in 2025.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: smartphones top export

new.s: What was India's rank in the IMD World Competitiveness ranking of 2025?
new.x: India's IMD Competitiveness rank improved from 43 (2021) to 41 (2025).
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: IMD competitiveness rank

new.s: Which State ranked first in BRAP 2017?
new.x: In BRAP 2017 AP was 1st, Telangana 2nd and Haryana 3rd.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: BRAP 2017 ranks

new.s: Which State ranked third in BRAP 2019, released on 5 September 2020?
new.x: BRAP 2019: AP 1st, UP 2nd, Telangana 3rd.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: BRAP 2019 third

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a category used in BRAP 2020?
new.x: BRAP 2020 used Top Achievers, Achievers, Aspirers and Emerging Business Ecosystems; 'Frontrunners' is a NITI Aayog category.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: BRAP 2020 categories

new.s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is the JSW Steel project of the Rayalaseema industrial hub?
new.x: The Rayalaseema hub includes JSW Steel at Kadapa, Kia and Royal Enfield at Tirupati.
new.angle: U0510 notes gap: JSW Steel Kadapa

new.s: On how many pillars is NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index based?
new.x: The NITI Index has 8 pillars, B-READY 3 pillars, Doing Business 10 parameters.
